def: Individually identifiable health information held or sent by a covered entity or its business associate, which HIPAA restricts and requires safeguards for.
The contract by which a vendor handling protected health information promises to safeguard it and accepts HIPAA's duties.
The HIPAA standard that only the protected health information needed for the purpose may be used or disclosed.
The HIPAA method of removing 18 listed kinds of identifier from health data, provided nothing else is known that could identify the person.
A tool that listens to a consultation, with consent, and drafts the clinical note for the clinician to review and sign.
Relevant content in the source that a generated summary leaves out, such as an allergy, and which a reviewer looking for wrong statements cannot see.
The habit of staff ignoring alerts because most are false, which can make a sensitive warning system unsafe in practice.
The tendency to follow a machine's suggestion even when one's own judgement would have been better.
Software that performs a medical purpose, such as diagnosis or treatment, without being part of a hardware device, and is regulated as a device.
The carve-out from the US device definition for software that gives recommendations to a clinician who can independently review the basis and that does not analyse images or signals.
A plan agreed with the FDA in advance describing which model changes a manufacturer may make, and how they are validated, without a new submission each time.
The precise role and scope of a model's output in a decision, against which its credibility must be shown.
